title: Forsgård–Shapiro coefficient-difference bound for real zeros
statement:
Let $f(z)=\sum_{k=0}^n a_kz^k$ be a polynomial with positive coefficients. Set $a_{-1}=a_{n+1}=0$ and

$$
\tilde c_k=(k+1)a_k^2-ka_{k-1}a_{k+1}.
$$

Let $0=k_1<k_2<\dots<k_m=n$ be the indices for which $\tilde c_{k_i}>0$, and let $v(f)$ be the number of changes in the sequence of parities $\{k_i\bmod 2\}_{i=0}^m$.

**Forsgård–Shapiro coefficient-difference conjecture.** The number of real zeros of $f$ does not exceed $v(f)$.

The source presents this as an open conjecture based on experimental motivation.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.05295

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2015). “Hawaiian`` conjecture was settled in by elementary but tedious calculations.”
source_name: B. Shapiro, “Problems around polynomials - the good, the bad and the ugly ...”, arXiv:1503.05295 (2015).
